title: Moth Italian-English code-switching speech dataset (v1.0.0)
description:
Scripted Italian speech with English words and phrases mixed in, recorded by three speakers for the Moth speech recognizer. 2,193 utterances, 1.46 hours, 48 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, with normalised transcripts, English word spans, categories and train/test/anchor splits.

The dataset is deliberately narrow: three speakers, read speech, quiet rooms. It is a benchmark and a fine-tuning seed, not a general-purpose code-switching corpus. The anchor split contains 60 test sentences read by every speaker; the test set is 600 clips (200 per speaker); the training split is 1,413 clips from two speakers. S3 never contributes to training.

Audio and transcripts are CC-BY-4.0. The speakers asked that their voices not be used for TTS/voice cloning or biometric identification; CC-BY-4.0 does not encode that restriction, so it is stated in the data card as an ethical request. Signed consent forms are held offline and are not part of the deposit.
notes: Audio and transcripts CC-BY-4.0; code Apache-2.0. The Hugging Face dataset is the canonical hosted copy. The companion model and paper are separate artifacts.
